candidates.title: Helping an Unconscious Stranger
candidates.description: WOMAN RESCUES UNCONSCIOUS STRANGER ON STREET WITH VID By Kiara Wells and Hannah Hodgetts Watch the courageous moment a woman rescued an unconscious teenage boy. While out for a walk with her daughter, 33-year-old Jodie Carnall noticed a teenager, Alfie, lying motionless on the pavement. Despite the boy’s friends calling out from across the street and insisting he was fine, Jodie immediately sensed something was wrong.  She rushed over and discovered Alfie was unconscious. Jodie quickly realised that Alfie had called emergency services himself but had been unable to respond over the phone as he was suffering from a seizure. As Alfie continued to seize, Jodie stayed by his side, performing first aid until paramedics arrived.  Jodie said: “I was walking with my daughter when I saw somebody lying on the ground from a distance.  “He wasn’t moving. I started recording just for my safety in case anything happened and I approached with caution as I had my daughter with me.  “As I got closer it became quite apparent that this young boy was having a seizure. “I performed first aid and called an ambulance. He had nine seizures in ten minutes whilst I waited for the ambulance.  “I held his head as it was viciously hitting the pavement during his seizures.  “Since then him and his mum have thanked me.” ENDS

The film is a feverish amalgamation of several stories by Edogawa Rampo (the pen name of horror and mystery writer Tarō Hirai), primarily drawing from “Strange Tale of Panorama Island” (Panorama-tō Kidan) and “The Demon of the Lonely Isle” (Kotō no Oni). The film follows Hirosuke (Teruo Yoshida), an amnesiac medical student trapped in an insane asylum, who escapes and assumes the identity of his doppelgänger, leading him to a remote island where a mad scientist performs grotesque experiments in an attempt to create a utopia of “ideal” humans. Notorious for its title and its controversial subject matter, the film was effectively banned in Japan for decades after its release. It is a key work of the Japanese “ero guro” (erotic-grotesque) movement and a precursor to the “pinky violence” style that would dominate Toei’s output in the early 1970s. candidates.title: The Final Moments of Budd Dwyer
candidates.description: Robert Budd Dwyer (November 21, 1939 – January 22, 1987) was an American politician. He served from 1971 to 1981 as a Republican member of the Pennsylvania State Senate representing the state's 50th district. He served as the 30th Treasurer of Pennsylvania from January 20th 1981, up until January 22nd 1987, the day of his suicide. In the early 1980s, Pennsylvania discovered its state workers had overpaid federal taxes due to errors in state withholding. Many accounting firms competed for a multimillion-dollar contract to determine compensation to each employee. In 1986, Dwyer was convicted of receiving a bribe from a California firm trying to gain the contract. Throughout his trial and after his conviction, he maintained that he was innocent of the charge and that he had been framed. Dwyer was scheduled to be sentenced on those charges on January 23, 1987, the day after his suicide. Nine news cameras recorded the events. A few witnesses who stood in the same room as Dwyer developed depression after the suicide and took breaks from journalism. Many schoolchildren witnessed the live broadcast due to most schools being closed due to snow. At the time, it was speculated that he may have killed himself to preserve pension benefits for his family, whose finances had been ruined by legal defense costs.  Dwyer was eventually found to be innocent six years later in 1993.

candidates.description: A group of people from the Busoga region gather at Makerere University, playing traditional drums in a powerful display of culture and unity. The performance highlights important rites and rituals surrounding traditional drumming practices. In Busoga tradition, drums are treated with great respect and are not placed directly on bare ground. Instead, a mat or cloth is first laid down, and the drums are placed on top of it. Different drums are played using specific techniques; some are beaten with sticks, while others, such as the ngalabi, are strictly played using hands. The way drums are played varies depending on the occasion. Rhythms used during moments of joy and celebration sound different from those used in times of sadness. In this video, the drumming expresses a moment of happiness.
